亓Bingkun Qi返回「关于我」的代表作

2018 · Physical Review Letters · First author · Original research

Why does light form a staircase?

Change just the waveguide at the edge of an array. How far into the array will the light reach?

My co-authors and I studied a row of waveguides with alternating gain and loss. Near the edge, a small change in one guide can trap a mode. Its light fades across the array, but on a logarithmic scale the intensity traces a staircase.

Read the guides in pairs, starting with 2 and 3. On one curve the two guides are equally bright. On the other, the first carries a quarter of its partner’s intensity. At fixed edge detuning and coupling, this ratio even survives changes in gain and loss, while the rate of fading across pairs can change.

This was my first project in Li Ge’s group, and finishing it gave me confidence as a researcher.
